BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline points

1. **The package departs from our playbook on almost every material term.** It shifts risk to Wattlebridge through low caps, high thresholds, short time limits, broad deemed disclosure and a buyer-knowledge bar. It also folds title, tax, IP and fraud into the general limitation regime.
2. **We should not accept the process framing.** The cover note says the positions were "settled at principal level", are "FINAL", reflect "market standard", and that clauses marked [STANDARD] were "cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny". These are the Seller's own assertions. Our playbook (secs 0.4 and 6.3) says we accept nothing as agreed, final or pre-cleared unless it is confirmed through our own authority process. I have reviewed every clause, including those marked [STANDARD]. The "efficiency note" should not limit our mark-up.
3. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its update on several points.** It says the Bluefen consent is not obtained and its conditions are not evidenced. It says the Riverlark facility is not repaid or discharged. It says the bonuses are not in the funds flow, and that the DD-006 incident scope is unknown. These are open completion risks, not settled items.
4. **The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 4 November 2026. We should request a refreshed position on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar before relying on any of it.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General Warranty cap (cl 12.1): Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Departure:** The Seller's figure equals our conditional fallback. That fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given. A matching number does not make the change cleared.
- **Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal that 20% is available.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the excess over the basket is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Effect:** The thresholds are five times our position. The deductible structure also means the Buyer permanently absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims.
- **Push back:** Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with a tipping basket. Thresholds must not apply to Fundamental/Title claims, specific indemnities or fraud.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **The sweep-in language matters more than the period.** It is a hidden general-regime override. It would apply general limitations to title, tax, IP, payment covenants, indemnities and fraud by default, unless we spot and expressly carve out each one.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the sweep-in sentence. Each limitation should apply only to the category it names.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Push back:** Reject outright. Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): "apply to all Claims of any nature"
- **Departure:** As drafted, this would extend caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all of these, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Push back:** Insert an express, overriding carve-out. Scope the non-reliance clause so it cannot operate as a defence to fraud. Note that some statutory remedies may not be excludable regardless of drafting. Litigation counsel should confirm the enforceability position under NSW and Commonwealth law.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2)
- **Seller:** It generally discloses the whole data room as at 22 September 2026, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. We reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosures must identify the specific warranty and give enough detail for the Buyer to assess the matter's nature and scope.
  - Confirm that the data room is not disclosed against Fundamental/Title warranties, specific indemnities or fraud.
- **Clause 1.4 (non-admission)** is acceptable in principle. It must not be read as qualifying any specific indemnity or covenant.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or anything "discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions.
- **Effect:** This is wider than a normal knowledge bar. Combined with general disclosure and the "discoverable" limb, it could neutralise most warranties.
- **Push back:** Delete. If a seller-knowledge qualifier appears elsewhere, it must name the seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Facts:** Per DD-002 and Disclosure Letter item 2, Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m). The change-control consent is in cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. No final consent or evidence that the conditions are met has been provided.
- **Playbook:** require effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not enough, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a Condition Precedent requiring an unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent in a form the Buyer approves.
  - Require documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
  - Give the Buyer a right to waive or terminate.
  - Upgrade the Seller's obligation from reasonable endeavours.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** a release "to be provided following Completion" for about AUD 3.2m outstanding.
- **Facts:** Per DD-003 and Disclosure Letter item 3, the facility is not repaid and no discharge is provided. There is a change-control clause at 8.1 and a discharge clause at 9.2.
- **Playbook:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Pay Riverlark directly from the funds flow and deduct the amount from the price as Debt.
  - Deliver executed deeds of release, PPSR discharge undertakings and the return of title documents at Completion.
  - Do not accept a post-completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's sign-off.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter item 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed.
- **Risk:** If the Company pays the bonuses after Completion, the Buyer bears them economically. "A matter for the Seller" does not say who pays.
- **Push back:**
  - Show the AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, any other employer costs) as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from price, or have them expressly Seller-funded.
  - Add a specific indemnity as a backstop.
  - Do not let the funds flow silently exclude them.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004 / DD-010)
- **Seller:** the indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate".
- **Facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but this is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
- **Push back:**
  - Extend the indemnity to cover:
    - failure of title to the Project Materials and related IP
    - third-party or Ironquay infringement claims
    - the costs of securing assignment or re-developing
    - related loss
  - Keep the cure route: payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees, then delivery of a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion covenant.
  - Ask for verification of the payment status. Do not assume the AUD 180,000 is owed or paid.
  - Keep this indemnity outside the general cap and thresholds.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Seller:** "a preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Facts:** Per Disclosure Letter item 6, a download link went to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification obligation are not established, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric amount in either direction.
- **Push back:**
  - Reject the "not expected to be material" characterisation. It is unsupported on the Seller's own disclosure.
  - Require pre-Completion covenants covering:
    - preservation of logs and evidence
    - a proper investigation (scope, access and recipient follow-up)
    - an assessment of notification obligations
    - regular updates to the Buyer
    - Buyer consultation before any regulator or individual communications
  - Consider a specific indemnity framework without pre-judging quantum.
  - Request a current status update, since the 22 September position is now about six weeks old.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011, AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** assess them. They are not automatically Debt and do not automatically reduce the price.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the ordinary-course label without information. Ask whether each renewal is:
  - unavoidable or terminable
  - accrued or prepaid
  - entered into in the ordinary course and at arm's length
  
  The Disclosure Letter flags them as "related" and says they should be read together for timing and scope. Decide on treatment (working capital, Debt, covenant or none) after review. Do not concede either way now.

### 14. Tax and IP warranties
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** these terms remain OPEN. Keep the categories separate. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Push back:** State expressly that tax and IP are not agreed and are not subject to the general regime by default.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Seller:** title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Playbook:** DD-012 is an internal source the Seller supplied, not independent proof. Disclosure Letter item 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence:
  - an ASIC company extract and share-structure history
  - share certificates and the transfer and issue history
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company
  - Seller board approvals and authority for the sale
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or other rights over shares exist
  - releases of any encumbrances over the shares

### 16. Other disclosed items (no Seller position stated, but to check)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** described as a notification obligation, not a landlord consent. Verify this ourselves and include the notification as a covenant or deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** described as an assignment restriction, not triggered by the share sale. Verify this independently, including any change-of-control language.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Counter 25% / AUD 6m (no authority for the fallback) |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping basket |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months + sweep-in | 24 months; delete the sweep-in |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | General regime | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside thresholds and knowledge bar |
| 5 | Fraud | Covered by limits and non-reliance | Full carve-out, non-waivable |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Delete |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | Condition Precedent: effective consent + evidence of cl 11.3 conditions |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not itemised | AUD 420k + on-costs as line item or Seller-funded |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Broaden indemnity; keep cure; verify the AUD 180k |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preservation, investigation and update covenants; no assumptions |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess; no automatic classification |
| 14 | Tax/IP | Settled | Open and separate |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence |

## Process actions
- **Reply to the Seller** that no clause is accepted as [STANDARD], cleared or final. Make clear our mark-up covers the whole package.
- **Check internally with Amelia Frost** whether any principal-level discussion took place, as the Seller claims. This is only to avoid being blindsided. Absent her written authority identifying this draft, the fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release) stay off the table.
- **Request refreshed facts** as at a current date on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment status, DD-006 and Sandbar, plus an updated data room index.
- **Treat the Seller's "market context"** (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months) as negotiating assertion, not authority.

- **Facts:** Per DD-003 and Disclosure Letter item 3, the facility is not repaid and no discharge is provided. There is a change-control clause at 8.1 and a discharge clause at 9.2.
- **Playbook:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Pay Riverlark directly from the funds flow and deduct the amount from the price as Debt.
  - Deliver executed deeds of release, PPSR discharge undertakings and the return of title documents at Completion.
  - Do not accept a post-completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's sign-off.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter item 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed.
- **Risk:** If the Company pays the bonuses after Completion, the Buyer bears them economically. "A matter for the Seller" does not say who pays.
- **Push back:**
  - Show the AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, any other employer costs) as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from price, or have them expressly Seller-funded.
  - Add a specific indemnity as a backstop.
  - Do not let the funds flow silently exclude them.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004 / DD-010)
- **Seller:** the indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate".
- **Facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers the SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but this is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
- **Push back:**
  - Extend the indemnity to cover:
    - failure of title to the Project Materials and related IP
    - third-party or Ironquay infringement claims
    - the costs of securing assignment or re-developing
    - related loss
  - Keep the cure route: payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees, then delivery of a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion covenant.
  - Ask for verification of the payment status. Do not assume the AUD 180,000 is owed or paid.
  - Keep this indemnity outside the general cap and thresholds.

### 12. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Seller:** "a preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Facts:** Per Disclosure Letter item 6, a download link went to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification obligation are not established, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric amount in either direction.
- **Push back:**
  - Reject the "not expected to be material" characterisation. It is unsupported on the Seller's own disclosure.
  - Require pre-Completion covenants covering:
    - preservation of logs and evidence
    - a proper investigation (scope, access and recipient follow-up)
    - an assessment of notification obligations
    - regular updates to the Buyer
    - Buyer consultation before any regulator or individual communications
  - Consider a specific indemnity framework without pre-judging quantum.
  - Request a current status update, since the 22 September position is now about six weeks old.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011, AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** assess them. They are not automatically Debt and do not automatically reduce the price.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the ordinary-course label without information. Ask whether each renewal is:
  - unavoidable or terminable
  - accrued or prepaid
  - entered into in the ordinary course and at arm's length
  
  The Disclosure Letter flags them as "related" and says they should be read together for timing and scope. Decide on treatment (working capital, Debt, covenant or none) after review. Do not concede either way now.

### 14. Tax and IP warranties
- **Seller:** "settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** these terms remain OPEN. Keep the categories separate. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Push back:** State expressly that tax and IP are not agreed and are not subject to the general regime by default.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Seller:** title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Playbook:** DD-012 is an internal source the Seller supplied, not independent proof. Disclosure Letter item 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence:
  - an ASIC company extract and share-structure history
  - share certificates and the transfer and issue history
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company
  - Seller board approvals and authority for the sale
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or other rights over shares exist
  - releases of any encumbrances over the shares
